reference: LibreOffice rendering the original .pub — the same libmspub parse our own extractor uses

metric.headline: score
metric.definition: Symmetric ink agreement at a placement tolerance of 1px: (matched reference ink + matched candidate ink) / (all reference ink + all candidate ink). An ink pixel matches when some ink pixel of the same colour exists in the other image within that radius.
metric.range: 0 = no mark in either image has a counterpart in the other; 1 = every mark does.
metric.ink: a pixel whose strongest channel is more than 32/255 away from white
metric.colour: ink colours match when the directions from white agree to within a cosine of 0.97 (~14 degrees), so antialiasing coverage is forgiven and hue is not
metric.placementTolerance: 1px at the render DPI; byRadius reports 0..2px so the reader can see how much of the score is tolerance
metric.pageSizeMismatch: images of different sizes are padded onto the union canvas with white, never scaled — a page emitted at the wrong size is meant to score badly
metric.perPixel: raw agreement over every pixel including the margins, at 0 and 16/255 per-channel slack; reported for reference only, since on a document page it is dominated by background
doesNotCapture: fidelity to Microsoft Publisher itself — the reference is LibreOffice rendering the same .pub, which shares our libmspub parser, so both sides inherit the same parse
text that is present but not selectable, searchable or editable: this compares pictures, not document structure
anything off the rasterised page area, including overset text pushed past the page edge
reading order, alt text, tagging and every other non-visual property
sub-pixel typographic differences below the ink threshold, such as slightly lighter hinting
